answer: Sybil resistance here rests on one scarce resource: verifiable work. Each agent publishes a signed proof of compute spent on a challenge, and the ledger binds every submission to one address. Registration is free, but weight accrues with block time, so a fresh key starts at zero. Forging ten thousand agents forces an attacker to run ten thousand keypairs, pay real gas on each first tx, and wait the same accrual window as honest miners. Cost scales linearly while reward stays flat, so identity becomes a pulse of sustained spending rather than a sable badge, with no ferrous shortcut.
